eips.title: In-mempool signature and proof aggregation
eips.summary: Extensive discussion on making frames forward compatible with 8288 aggregation, likely removing the signature list.

moments.context: Lightclient introduced EIP-8288 as a major outcome from the DevCon Mumbai breakout, describing it as the future aggregation scheme for PQ signatures and ZK proofs in blocks.
Discussion of how 8288 introduces a new frame mode and is at odds with the current signature list approach, and whether to extend the signature list or adopt a new proof frame mode.
Lightclient emphasized the two large spec changes needed before year-end: removing the signature list for 8288 forward compatibility, and deciding on SSZ serialization.
Iván agreed 8288 is too big for Hegota but supports splitting it and shipping a minimal forward-compatible piece now, with a draft proposal coming soon.
Lightclient stated the main goal is that users should not have to change their wallet again when aggregation via 8288 eventually ships.
Toni described how 8288 transactions would come with a sidecar containing signatures, and suggested shipping the sidecar separation before aggregation.
Lightclient confirmed the signature list PR was a quick fix but the right approach is making frames forward compatible with 8288, which is harder.

eips.title: Transaction Assertions via State Diff Opcode
eips.summary: Discussed interaction with paymastered frame transactions where assert could revert paymaster payments.

moments.context: Lightclient explained that 7906 transaction assertions conflict with paymastered frame transactions because assert reverts all execution frames including the paymaster payment.
Lightclient said he disliked proposed workarounds like non-revertible frame flags, and suggested 7906 may simply not work with paymaster transactions in the public mempool initially.

eips.title: Set Code for EOAs
eips.summary: Referenced as the mechanism for converting EOAs to smart accounts before migrating to PQ signers.

moments.context: Ryan described the ideal flow as 7702 converting EOAs to smart accounts, removing ecrecover, and permanently converting to frame transactions with new PQ signers.
Daniil noted in chat that 8151 exempts 7702 delegation indicators, so plain 7702 keeps old permits alive even with 8151.

eips.title: Account Code Restricted ecRecover
eips.summary: Identified as a priority alongside frames for PQ readiness, restricting ecrecover to retire K1 permits.

moments.context: Daniil explained in chat that 8151 exempts 7702 delegation indicators, so old permits stay live under plain 7702; paired with the EIP-8141 PR that installs real code, 8151 kills K1 permits for the full retirement path.
Guru identified 8151 (restricted ecrecover) and SETCODEFROM as the PQ priorities alongside frames that still need hardening before adding more EIPs.

eips.title: Reject transactions from senders with deployed code
eips.summary: Cited in chat as the rule that kills K1 transactions once real code is installed via SETCODEFROM.

moments.context: Daniil noted in chat that the EIP-8141 set-code-from PR installs real code, so EIP-3607 kills K1 transactions, complementing 8151 which kills K1 permits.

eips.title: SETCODEFROM Code Reuse Instruction
eips.summary: Named alongside 8151 as a PQ readiness priority needing further hardening work.

moments.context: Guru listed SETCODEFROM (8298) together with 8151 as the EIPs that still need hardening before the team takes on additional proposals.

eips.title: Frame Transaction
eips.summary: Two open PRs discussed: raising MAX_VERIFY_GAS to 300K, and setting code from the default code in SENDER mode.

moments.context: Daniil presented two PRs updating EIP-8141: one for migration using set code from, and one raising the default verify gas limit from 100K to 300K based on Nethermind benchmarks.
Besu expressed support for the 300K max verify gas increase, noting they hit the same limits in fuzzing, though they want to run it by performance folks.
Toni cautioned that increasing max verify gas also impacts builders in the critical path for FOCIL inclusion list checking, not just the mempool.
Iván asked whether to ship 8141 with 100K or wait; Toni suggested it may be too early to lock in a gas limit before Hegota scope is decided.

eips.title: VOPS Profiles for FOCIL Eligibility
eips.summary: Justin Zen proposed splitting VOPS verification into STATE and non-STATE to remove the claimed index problem.

moments.context: Justin Zen explained that 8369 requires builders to provide an index for omission checks, a weaker assumption than blobs, and proposed caching the non-state proof check to enable end-of-block verification like normal blobs.
